indicator: % of children who received child protection services
definition: The percentage of children who participated in GN child protection programs in the community.
methodOfCalculation: (Number of children receiving specific child protection services / Total number of children in the community) × 100
methods: Number of children receiving specific child protection services (numerator) is equal to the value for "1.1. # of children who received child protection services."
notes: The number of children receiving specific child protection services is equal to the value for "1.1. # of children who received child protection services."

indicator: 1.1. # of children who received child protection services
definition: The total number of children in the community who participated in GN child protection programs
methodOfCalculation: Sum of children receiving specific child protection services
methods: Case management records, service delivery logs, etc.
notes: Examples of child protection programs include direct provision of child case management support (psychosocial support, legal aid, safe shelter, or family tracing and reunification), connecting children to local services, formation of child protection groups, and implementation of education programs on child abuse, violence, discrimination, and other threats for the public (including children and stakeholders).

indicator: 1.1.1. # of children with new birth registration
definition: Please count the number of births newly registered in the reporting year. Birth registration is the process of officially recording a child's birth in the civil registry by a government authority.

indicator: 1.1.2. # of children at risk who were referred to specialised services by GN
definition: The total number of identified children at risk formally linked by staff or partners to targeted, advanced interventions (e.g., clinical mental health, legal aid, specialized medical care, or state welfare) that exceed standard case management.
methodOfCalculation: Number of children referred to specialized services
notes: Children identified as facing specific child protection threats or vulnerabilities. This includes unaccompanied and separated children (UASC), survivors of abuse or gender-based violence (GBV), children in hazardous labor, or children experiencing severe psychosocial distress. Targeted interventions that exceed standard community-based support or general case management. Examples include clinical mental health and psychiatric care, specialised medical or clinical care (e.g., clinical management of rape), legal aid and justice services, formal alternative care placements or state welfare interventions, and others.

indicator: 1.2. # of people participating in child rights programs (1.2.2 + 1.2.3 + 1.2.4  - Duplicates)
definition: The total number of people who participated in activities or programs supported by GN aimed at raising awareness or promoting child rights
methodOfCalculation: Sum of participants from all GN child rights activities or programs
methods: Attendance lists, registration forms, or activity reports

indicator: 1.2.1. # of children’s, teens’ or youth clubs supported by GN
definition: The total number of children’s, teens’, or youth clubs actively supported by GN programs.
methodOfCalculation: Count of actively supported clubs.
methods: Club registration lists, program reports, etc.
notes: N/A

indicator: 1.2.2. # of members in children’s, teens’ or youth clubs supported by GN
definition: The total number of active members across all children’s, teens’, or youth clubs supported by GN.
methodOfCalculation: Sum of active members from all supported clubs
methods: Club membership lists, attendance records, or participant registration forms
notes: N/A

indicator: 1.2.3. # of children and adults who have participated in child rights campaign activities
definition: The total number of children and adults who participated in child rights campaign activities supported by GN.
methodOfCalculation: Sum of participants from all GN-supported child-led rights campaign activities.
methods: Campaign attendance lists, registration forms, or activity reports.
notes: Campaign activities may include public awareness events, social media campaigns, forums, workshops that children primarily designed and implemented.

indicator: 1.2.4. # of adults trained on child rights, child protection and safeguarding
definition: The total number of adults who completed training programs focusing on child rights, child protection, and safeguarding principles and practices.
methodOfCalculation: Sum of all adults who completed GN-supported training programs.
methods: Training attendance lists, completion certificates, or participant registration forms.
notes: N/A

indicator: 1.3. # of community- and/or child-led initiatives that influence child-related decisions at the community, regional or national level
definition: The total number of initiatives led by children and/or community that aim to influence specific child-related decisions or policies at the community, regional, or national level.
methodOfCalculation: Count of activities such as: Issues raised by children are formally included on meeting agendas with government or local authorities Official written or recorded responses are received from government or local authorities Children’s views or recommendations are reflected in policy documents, government reports, or official meeting minutes
methods: Use reports, meeting minutes, or news articles
notes: “Child-led” initiatives refer to activities that are initiated, designed, or primarily implemented by children. These may include consultations with decision-makers, petitions, campaigns, or advocacy actions that lead to documented government consideration or response.

indicator: 1.4. # of activities that aimed at strengthening child rights or child protection-related laws, policies or budgets at a regional or national or international level
definition: The total number of distinct advocacy or policy engagement activities that aimed at strengthening child rights or child protection-related laws, policies, or budgets at a regional, national, or international level.
methodOfCalculation: Count of all relevant activities at the country head office.
methods: Use GN advocacy reports, policy briefs, government documents, etc.
notes: Examples include Regional level: Participating in regional forums on child protection legislation National level: Joining or forming national networks for policy advocacy International level examples: Contributing to a UN report or participating in international policy discussions on child rights

indicator: 1.5. # of people who participated in GN Child Protection advoacy
definition: Please count the number people who participated in any type of GN's advocacy activities on protection.

indicator: # of child rights advocacy activities
definition: The total number of distinct activities aimed at advocating for the promotion, protection, or fulfilment of child rights.
methodOfCalculation: Count of all distinct child rights advocacy activities.
methods: Activity reports or meeting logs.
notes: Child rights advocacy activities may include on/offline seminars, forums, campaigns, education, or policy discussions, etc. Child’s clubs are recorded under other indicators.

indicator: # of local leaders & volunteers involved in child right & protection monitoring
definition: The total number of local leaders and volunteers who are actively involved in GN-supported child rights and protection monitoring activities.
methodOfCalculation: Count of actively engaged local leaders and volunteers.
methods: Meeting attendance records, activity logs, or program reports.
notes: N/A

indicator: # of local-led submissions or engagements related to child-related policies (e.g., submission of local ordinances, partnerships with local governments)
definition: The total number of documented initiatives where local entities (e.g., community groups) led submissions or engagements with relevant authorities to influence child-related policies or decisions.
methodOfCalculation: Count of documented local-led submissions or engagements.
methods: Policy proposals, policy briefs or any other written opinions delivered to decision makers or partnership documents.
notes: Examples include submission of local ordinances or formal partnerships with local governments on child-related issues. “Local-led” implies significant initiative from local actors.

indicator: % of NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training) (Gender marker)
definition: The percentage of young people of secondary school age in a defined target area who are not currently participating in education, formal employment, or vocational training.
methodOfCalculation: (Number of secondary-school-aged NEETs in target population / Total number of secondary-school-aged young people in target population) × Survey Weight × 100
methods: Household surveys.
notes: Use the age range of 15-24 specifically.

indicator: % of people who have completed upper secondary schools or above
definition: The percentage of the target population who have successfully completed upper secondary education or any higher level of education.
methodOfCalculation: (Number of individuals in target population who completed upper secondary or above / Total target population) × Survey Weight × 100
methods: Household surveys
notes: “Target population” may include individuals aged 18–24. Depending on the national education system, the relevant age range may be higher or lower (e.g. 19+ in countries where upper secondary programmes are longer). Higher education may include vocational or technical education as well as tertiary education.

indicator: School completion rate (primary and lower secondary school, separately) (Gender marker)
definition: The percentage of students enrolled in the first grade of a given education level (primary or lower secondary) who eventually complete the final grade of that same level.
methodOfCalculation: (Number of students completing final grade of level / Number of students enrolled in first grade of same level X years ago) × 100
methods: Use secondary data (e.g. village- or district-level data from local government or education authorities)
notes: Where administrative data are unavailable, household surveys may be conducted. Data collection is limited to target schools within our catchment areas.

indicator: % of children transitioning from primary to lower secondary education (Gender marker)
definition: Percentage of primary school graduates who enroll in lower secondary education in the subsequent academic year.
methodOfCalculation: (Number of primary graduates enrolled in lower secondary / Total number of primary school graduates) × 100
methods: Secondary data (e.g., school enrollment records, district-level education statistics).
notes: Data collection is limited to target schools within our catchment areas.

indicator: School attendance rate (SDG 4.1.2; secondary data)
definition: Percentage of children who attend school on a regular basis.
methodOfCalculation: (Number of children attending schools/Total number of children) × 100
methods: Use secondary data (e.g. village- or district-level data from local government)
notes: Provide primary school attendance rate and lower secondary school attendance rate separately. Use nationally defined ages for primary school and lower secondary school. Regular attendance is generally over 90%. Data collection is limited to target schools within our catchment areas.

indicator: Under-five mortality rate (per 1000 live births) (SDG 3.2.1) (Gender marker)
definition: # of deaths of children under age 5 per 1,000 live births in the target area
methodOfCalculation: (Number of deaths among children under 5 during the reference period ÷ Number of live births during the same period) × 1,000
methods: Use secondary data (e.g. health data from local government)
notes: Where administrative data are unavailable, use household surveys such as DHS or MICS at the most relevant geographical level and survey rounds.

indicator: (Well-being) Improvement in subjective well-being
definition: Level of self-reported well-being among the target population, measured using standardized survey questions
methodOfCalculation: Average subjective well-being score calculated from standardized survey questions
methods: Use household surveys
notes: Ensure the same question wording, response scale, and survey method are used across survey rounds to allow valid comparison. Example questions may include: (Life Satisfaction) “All things considered, how satisfied are you with your life as a whole these days?” (Happiness) “Overall, how happy did you feel yesterday?” (Anxiety) “Overall, how anxious did you feel yesterday?” (Worthwhile) “Overall, to what extent do you feel that the things you do in your life are worthwhile?”.

methods: Calculation by head offices

indicator: % of health facilities with essential infrastructure (basic amenities, infection prevention, trained staff, etc.)
definition: The percentage of health facilities that meet criteria for essential infrastructure, including basic amenities, infection prevention measures, and the presence of trained staff
methodOfCalculation: (Number of facilities meeting criteria/ Total number of facilities supported in a target area) × 100
methods: Facility assessments, checklists, or inspection reports
notes:
Number of facilities meeting criteria is equal to the value for "3.1.1. # of health facilities with essential infrastructure (basic amenities, infection prevention, trained staff, etc.)built, renovated and/or maintained"

Facilities are considered to meet minimum requirements if they satisfy at least 80% of the criteria listed below: Improved water source (see definition in ID 3.4) Reliable electricity supply (grid, generator, or solar) Functional handwashing facilities with soap and water Availability of basic personal protective equipment (PPE) At least one qualified health worker present during operating hours.

indicator: % increase in household income of social economic organization members
definition: Percentage change in average household income among members of GN-supported social economy organizations compared with baseline.
methodOfCalculation: % income increase = (Real household income at endline - Real household income at baseline) / Real household income at baseline * 100
methods: Member surveys collecting self-reported income data (at baseline and endline).
notes: Target cooperative members. Income includes all major sources (e.g. wages, self-employment, business income, etc.). A baseline survey may be conducted in Year 1 and an endline survey in Year 5. Real income is obtained by dividing nominal income by the national Consumer Price Index (CPI). Adjust for inflation and report income in real terms where feasible. **Sector**** ****5**** ****Climate change response and sustainable environment**** **

definition: Total number of GN-supported social economy organizations operating during the reporting period
methodOfCalculation: Count of active social economy organizations.
methods: Project records, registration documents, etc.
notes: Report figures separately for cooperatives and social enterprises.

indicator: # of participants in biz cooperatives, separately
# of new business proposals developed by cooperatives
definition: Total number of new business proposals developed by GN-supported cooperatives during the reporting period
methodOfCalculation: Count of completed business proposals
methods: Review submitted business proposals
notes: Proposals may include business expansion plans.

indicator: Employment generated by social economic organizations
definition: Total number of jobs directly created by GN-supported cooperatives or social enterprises during the reporting period
methodOfCalculation: Count of individuals employed by cooperatives or social enterprises
methods: Employment registers, etc.
notes: Include full-time and part-time positions, as well as existing jobs and newly hired positions.

indicator: # of local or national climate-related policies on climate adaptation/mitigation and biodiversity directly or indirectly affected by GN advocacy efforts.
definition: Stipulated policies such as legislation, regulations, funding or initiatives that show governments’ commitment to climate mitigation, carbon reduction and environment protection, such as NDC, long-term strategies, national adaptation plans or communication/public engagement strategies
methodOfCalculation: Count/list of climate-related regulations at the national/local levels.
methods: Case reports, policy documents, environmental regulations/laws.
notes: May need to identify relevant local/national policies that incorporate GN’s climate mitigation or carbon reduction models

indicator: % of households adopting low-carbon practices or using low-carbon energy technologies as a result of GN support (Gender marker)
definition: The proportion of households that have adopted low-carbon practices or use low-carbon energy sources
methodOfCalculation: (Households adopting low-carbon practices/technologies) / (Total number of beneficiaries of low-carbon devices) * (Survey weights) * 100
methods: Survey
notes: Disaggregate by vulnerable group (women/children/extremely poor etc. as defined by GN)

indicator: % of people contributing to community-wide climate adaptation and mitigation activities
definition: Percentage of people that participated in community-wide climate adaptation and mitigation activities through GN’s interventions/support, such as forest management, recycling & resource management, community agriculture infrastructure etc.
methodOfCalculation: (Number of participants in GN's community-led initiatives for climate adaptation or mitigation / Total number of people in the community) × 100
notes: The number of participants in GN's community-led initiatives for climate adaptation or mitigation is equal to the value for "5.1. # of people contributing to community-wide climate adaptation and mitigation activities (5.1.1 + 5.1.2 + 5.1.3 - Duplicates)."

indicator: Total surface (hectare) under GN environment programmes
definition: The total surface area that benefited from GN’s environmental protection programmes, including reforestation, ecological restoration, forest preservation, or habitat protection programmes, land degradation prevention, drought resilience, climate resilient water resource management etc.
methodOfCalculation: Sum of the mapped area (in hectares) of all land/sites covered by GN environment programmes.
methods: GIS/remote sensing, Record of programme sites, Program report, GIF measures

indicator: 5.1. # of people contributing to community-wide climate adaptation and mitigation activities (5.1.1 + 5.1.2 + 5.1.3 - Duplicates)
definition: The total number of people that participated in community-wide climate adaptation and mitigation activities through GN’s interventions/support, such as forest management, recycling & resource management, community agriculture infrastructure etc.
methodOfCalculation: Sum of participants in GN’s community-led initiatives for climate adaptation/mitigation.
methods: Program report, beneficiary list, community initiatives.
notes: Disaggregate by age, gender and vulnerability to measure the proportion of vulnerable populations among beneficiaries; To distinguish from ID 5.1.4, climate adaptation/mitigation programmes mean interventions that involve actual adaptation/mitigation activities (e.g., better irrigation or drainage infrastructure etc.) beyond awareness campaigns

indicator: 5.1.1. # of people (farmers, fishers, traders or community members) using low-carbon/eco-friendly/energy-efficient devices provided by GN
definition: The total number of farmers, fishermen, or traders who adopted GN’s low-carbon devices in their livelihoods.
methodOfCalculation: Count of farmers/fishers/forest people actively using low-carbon devices
methods: Program report.

indicator: 5.1.2. # of households that established and regularly practice GN-supported renewable resource management activities
definition: The total number of households that established GN-supported renewable resource management activities such as waste sorting for recycling, composting, water reuse, food waste processing or other resource-efficiency practices.
methodOfCalculation: (Count of households practising renewable resource management activities) / (Total number of households in climate campaigns/training) * 100
methods: Program report; beneficiary records.
notes: At the mid-term level, sustainable practice means simple behaviour change at the individual/household level that does not involve affordability or supply-side issues. “People practising renewable resource management” may require a simple survey (e.g., “Does your household have a renewable resource management system?”)

indicator: 5.1.3. # of farms, fisheries or forest-dependent households adopting GN-supported sustainable production practices
definition: The proportion of farms, fisheries or forest-dependent households who adopted GN-supported sustainable production practices, such as climate-smart agriculture, sustainable fishing, forest management, clean energy use, or resource-efficient practices
methodOfCalculation: (Farms/fisheries/forest-dependent-households that adopted sustainable production practices) / (Entire participating farms/fisheries/forest-dependent households) * 100
methods: Beneficiary records

indicator: 5.1.4. # of people who completed GN-supported climate awareness, environmental protection campaigns or education/training activities
definition: The total number of people who completed climate and environment-related campaigns, education/training activities through GN
methodOfCalculation: Sum of participants who completed GN climate/environment education/campaigns
methods: Count of completion certificates, participant list (registration form)
notes: Includes climate/environment awareness activities in forest management, clean energy, recycling & resource management, and agriculture etc.

indicator: 5.2. # of people (farmers, fishers, traders or community members) who received GN-supported training for in climate-adaptive and environmentally friendly livelihood practice
definition: The total number of people who received training for a transition towards low-carbon lifestyles such as nature-based solutions, climate resilient crops, water resource management, or sustainable farming etc.
methodOfCalculation: Count of people who received climate adaptation training
methods: Beneficiary records

indicator: 5.3. # of advocacy activities that aim to improve government policy for climate mitigation/adaptation and environmental protection
definition: The total number of GN’s advocacy activities that aim to improve government policy directions towards sustainable environment
methodOfCalculation: Count/list of climate advocacy activities
methods: Qualitative case report.

indicator: 5.4. # of people who participated in GN environment and climate change advoacy
definition: Please count the number people who participated in any type of GN's advocacy activities on environment.

indicator: 5.5. # of formal partnership agreements established with local stakeholders to coordinate and jointly implement climate resilience and environmental sustainability activities
definition: The total number/list of partnership agreements signed with local stakeholders (UN agencies, private investors, governments, academia, NGOs etc.) for joint implementation of climate resilience/environmental sustainability projects
methodOfCalculation: Count/list of partnership agreements with local stakeholders.
methods: Partnership documentation such as MoU list, joint workplan, collaboration documentation

indicator: # of community members aware of climate risks
definition: The total number of community members who are aware of climate risks after participating in GN climate campaigns
methodOfCalculation: Survey during interventions (climate knowledge score or self-reported awareness) or the number of participants who successfully completed the GN climate training
methods: Survey; program reports
notes: Sample questions include: - (self-awareness) To what extent are you aware of climate risks affecting your community? (1 to 5) - (self-awareness) To what extent are you aware of the actions you need to take to stay safe from those risks? (1 to 5) - (self-awareness) To what extent are you aware where you can access early warnings? - (knowledge score) List/select any climate risks affecting your community - (knowledge score) List/select actions to stay safe during those risks - (knowledge score) Where can you access early warnings?

indicator: # of eco-friendly projects strengthening eco-systems and nature-based solutions against climate change
definition: The total number of GN climate ecosystem (including mitigation and carbon reduction) in the implementation phase, including a) community-based climate initiatives, b) Nature-based Solution projects, c) energy transition projects, d) all other projects, and e) pilot or demo sites identified/selected for longer-term mitigation projects, on reforestation, mangrove protection/restoration or green infrastructure for watershed etc.
methodOfCalculation: Count of relevant projects.
methods: Program report, project list

indicator: # of public infrastructures built or rehabilitated for climate resilience against floods, tropical storms, heatwaves etc. (annual and accumulated)
definition: The total number of infrastructure/public facilities (schools, community centres, health posts, bridges, roads, channels, reservoirs etc.) built or rehabilitated for climate resilience.
methodOfCalculation: Count of facilities/infrastructure included in construction/rehabilitation projects
methods: Program report.

indicator: Presence of local/national strategies for disaster management and disaster risk reduction
definition: Local or national policies or regulations that stipulate long-term disaster management or risk reduction strategies
methodOfCalculation: Count & list of all relevant policies, strategies, or regulations
methods: Secondary data (policies/regulations)
notes: N/A

indicator: # of people covered by or with access to national/local humanitarian response system/mechanism
definition: Total number people (individuals) that are monitored by national/local humanitarian response system/mechanism, such as early warning systems or disaster risk information
methodOfCalculation: Count of individuals covered by humanitarian response systems
methods: Secondary data
notes: Alternative indicator can be ‘# of local governments having a plan to act on early warnings’ (G-4 Sendai Framework)

indicator: 6.1. # of people who participated in disaster risk reduction (DRR) or anticipatory action (AA) activities
definition: Total number of people who participated in GN’s DRR/AA programmes
methodOfCalculation: Sum of DRR/AR participants
methods: Headcounts based on attendance lists or registration forms
notes: N/A

indicator: 6.2. # of people who benefited from emergency relief programmes, including natural disasters, conflicts and climate crisis (6.2.1 + 6.2.2 + 6.2.3 + 6.2.5 + 6.2.6 - Duplicates)
definition: Individuals or households that received GN’s emergency relief programmes in all forms and project areas
methodOfCalculation: Count of all program beneficiaries
methods: Headcounts from registration records.

indicator: 6.2.1. # of people who received food assistance
definition: Please count the number of people who received food assistance by GN as a humanitarian response.

indicator: 6.2.2. # of people who received non-food item (NFI) kits
definition:
Please count the number of people who received non-food items (NFI) by GN as a humanitarian response.
The most common items for NFI may include bedding equipment, kitchen utensils, hygiene material, clothes, heating and lighting equipment, and more. Please make sure not to include the number of shelters those are collected in '6.2.4' separately.

indicator: 6.2.3. # of people who received cash and/or voucher assistance
definition: Please count the number of people who received cash and/or vouncher by GN as a humanitarian reponse.

indicator: 6.2.4. # of households provided with shelters
definition: Please count the number of established shelters that meet the standards set by the National Shelter Cluster/Government as a humanitarian response.

indicator: 6.2.5. # of people who received psychosocial support (PSS) activities
definition:
Please count the number of people who received psychosocial support (PSS) activities by GN as a humanitarian response.
Psychosocial support refers to actions that meet psychological and social needs of individuals, families and communities. Psychosocial support during emergencies should ensure safety and promote calm, connectedness, and personal and collective efficacy, and hope.

indicator: 6.2.6. # of people who received gender-based violence (GBV) related support and/or case management
definition:
Please count the number of people who received gender-based violence (GBV) related support and/or case management by GN as a humanitarian response.
Gender-based violence is violence against a person because of that person's gender or violence that affects persons of a particular gender disproportionately. The activities to address the GBV cases involve training, rehabilitation, campaigns, men's involvement, and more.

indicator: 6.3. # of participants in refugees/internally displaced persons (IDP) support programs in protracted situations (6.3.1 + 6.3.2 + 6.3.3 + 6.3.4 - Duplicates)
definition: The total number of people who participated in GN’s refugee/IDP support programmes
methodOfCalculation: Count of individuals in refugee/IDP support programmes
methods: Headcounts based on program records.
notes: Disaggregate at the information collection level (e.g., refugee female/male; IDP female/male; host community female/male etc.)

indicator: 6.3.1. # of people who participated in refugee/host community livelihoods programs
definition: Please count the number of people who participated in livelihood programs by GN as a refugee/IDP response.

indicator: 6.3.2. # of people participated in peacebuilding or social cohesion activities
definition: Total number of refugees/IDPs and host community members who participated in peacebuilding/social-cohesion programmes
methodOfCalculation: Sum of peacebuilding/social-cohesion programme participants
methods: Program attendance lists or registration forms
notes: N/A

indicator: 6.3.3. # of people (households) who benefitted from rehabilitation projects
definition: Total number of individuals (or households) in areas or settlements that benefitted from GN’s rehabilitation projects
methodOfCalculation: Sum of individuals in reconstruction/rehabilitation areas
methods: Population data, project records.
notes: Infrastructure reconstruction and all other rehabilitation

indicator: 6.3.4. # of people who participated in GN emergency relief & disaster risk reduction advoacy
definition: Please count the number people who participated in any type of GN's advocacy activities on emergency relief and disaster risk reduction.

indicator: % of refugees/IDPs integrated into social/economic systems (host or original communities)
definition: Total percentage (or number) of GN’s refugee/IDP beneficiaries who have access to social or economic systems
methodOfCalculation: (Number of refugee beneficiaries with ‘integration status’)/(Number of total refugee beneficiaries) * 100 (see notes for specific status)
methods: Program attendance lists or registration forms, refugee profile records
notes: divide into % of refugees with decent jobs (may need to define what a ‘decent’ job means); % of refugee children enrolled in the national education system; % of refugees (or refugee households) with access to national healthcare systems. Alternatively, % of refugees who benefited from economic integration projects (e.g., employed in farms etc.)

indicator: % of reported conflicts resolved through community-based conflict resolution or mediation mechanisms
definition: Proportion of cases where conflicts are resolved through GN’s community-based mediation mechanisms
methodOfCalculation: (# of conflicts resolved through community-based mechanisms)/(Total incidents of conflicts identified and intervened by GN) * 100
methods: Program records
notes: N/A

indicator: % of reported disasters and/or conflicts responded through community-driven preparedness and response mechanisms
definition: Proportion of all reported disaster/conflicts that were resolved through community-driven preparedness and response mechanisms
methodOfCalculation: (# of reported disaster/conflict incidents responded through community-driven preparedness and response mechanisms) / (total # of reported disaster/conflict incidents) * 100
methods: Program (case) report & records
notes: N/A

indicator: # of children and adults who participated in GN refugee protection programs
# of refugee children who participated in GN education programmes
Community Index built by GN
definition: A composite index measuring social cohesion and sense of community in areas where GN has been supported
methodOfCalculation: A standardized composite score based on selected indicators. The index is constructed by selecting key items, testing reliability and validity, and standardizing scores to allow comparison across locations.
methods: Household surveys
notes: Example items include: (Participation) # of GN volunteers; # of committees and sub-committees (Inclusiveness) % of females in committees or sub-committees (Community governance) # of agenda items decided in committee meetings; average number of committee meetings per year (Movement) # of GN global or national campaign participants (Ownership) Financial value of community contribution 27 | | | | | --- | --- | --- |

indicator: 7.1. # of committees and sub-committees formally established and actively operating
definition: Total number of committees and sub-committees that are established and actively operating
methodOfCalculation: Count of committees and sub-committees that meet the “active” criteria.
methods: Committee regulations or documents
notes: Include both existing and newly established committees. Record committees (7.1.1) and sub-committees (7.1.2) separately. Examples of sub-committees may include WASH committees, health committees, and education committees, etc.

indicator: 7.1.1. # of committees
7.1.2. # of sub-committees
7.2. # of active members of committees and sub-committees (Gender marker)
definition: Total number of individuals who are active members of committees and sub-committees
methodOfCalculation: Count of members recorded as active.
methods: Membership lists, attendance records.
notes: Please specify the percentage of youth, elderly, and ethnic minority members as 7.2.1.

indicator: 7.2.1. # of active members of committees and sub-committees (Gender marker)
7.3. # of GN volunteers engaged in programme activities
definition: The number of volunteers who participated in activities/services/programs/projects operated by GN
methodOfCalculation: Count of volunteers recorded as active
methods: Use activity logs, attendance sheets or program reports.
notes: N/A

indicator: 7.4. # of training sessions for committee or sub-committee members
definition: Total number of training sessions conducted to build the capacities of committee or sub-committee members
methodOfCalculation: Count of completed training sessions.
methods: Training reports, attendance sheets
notes: Trainings may include governance, leadership, technical, or financial management topics.

indicator: 7.5. # of meetings held by committees and sub-committees
definition: Total number of meetings formally held by committees and sub-committees
methodOfCalculation: Count of meetings documented.
methods: Meeting minutes or committee records.
notes: Include regular and extraordinary meetings.

indicator: 7.6. # of activities decided by community committees and sub-committees in the following year's GN Plan of Action (POA)
definition: Total number of agenda items formally discussed and decided by community committees and sub-committees during the reporting period.
methodOfCalculation: Count of agenda items with documented decisions.
methods: Meeting minutes, resolutions, or committee records
notes: Include only items with documented decisions. Examples include: - Approval of community development plans or annual action plans - Decisions on allocation or use of community or project resources - Adoption of community rules, by-laws, or operating procedures - Project strategies, such as priorities, activities, or beneficiary selection criteria

indicator: 7.7. Financial value of community contribution (volunteer labour, in-kind, cash, land) to project implementation
definition: Estimated total monetary value (in USD) of community contributions to GN-supported project implementation, including volunteer labour, in-kind contributions, cash, or land.
methodOfCalculation: Sum of the estimated monetary value of all community contributions
methods: financial records, contribution certificates, etc.
notes: If the amount is already recorded as income in the financial accounting system, use the recorded value. Examples include: Volunteer labour hours × standard hourly rate Market value of in-kind goods or materials Cash contributions received Estimated market value of land contributed

indicator: 7.8. # of local or national policies or regulations or laws initiated or influenced by Good Neighbors
definition: Total number of local or national policies, regulations, or laws that GN initiated, contributed to, or significantly influenced
methodOfCalculation: Count of policies, regulations, or laws documented
methods: Policy documents, government publications, media releases, and related official records.
notes: GN influence may include technical input, policy recommendations, participation in drafting committees or consultations, evidence submission, or advocacy activities. Count each policy or legal instrument once, even if GN contributed through multiple activities.

indicator: 7.9. # of people who participated in GN gender equality and women's rights advoacy
definition: - Please count the number people who participated in any type of GN's advocacy activities on gender equality and women' rights.

indicator: MOUs signed with partner organizations
definition: Total number of Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) formally signed between GN and partner organizations during the reporting period.
methodOfCalculation: Count of signed MOUs
methods: Signed agreements, legal or administrative records.
notes: The number of both new and continued cooperation agreements (including a memorandum of understanding (MOU)), with private, public, and nonprofit organizations from various fields with common goals that commit to work together and share resources.

indicator: # of capacity-building sessions delivered to strengthen community leadership
definition: Total number of capacity-building sessions delivered to enhance leadership, governance, or organizational skills of community leaders
methodOfCalculation: Count of completed capacity-building sessions
methods: Training reports, attendance records, or program documentation.
notes: Sessions may include leadership development, conflict resolution, or community development planning for non-committee members.

indicator: # of regional or national or global alliance networks joined as a member
definition: Total number of regional, national, or global alliance networks in which GN holds formal membership
methodOfCalculation: Count the number of any forms of networks, associations, coalitions, working groups, or clusters by sectors that the GN is officially registered and contributes to the coalition's collaborative mission/project/work as a member at the regional or national, or global level
methods: Membership records
notes: The number of regional, national, or global alliance networks related to policy, development projects, and humanitarian assistance to which GN has joined and is active. Being active means paying dues, submitting required reports, attending meetings, or participating in working group activities during the year

indicator: # of launched global or national campaigns (accumulated)
definition: Total cumulative number of global or national advocacy or awareness campaigns launched by GN
methodOfCalculation: Cumulative count of campaigns launched
methods: Campaign reports, advocacy reports, etc.
notes: Campaigns may include public awareness, advocacy, fundraising, or other initiatives. Count each campaign once at launch.

indicator: # of global or national campaign participants
definition: Total number of individuals who participated in GN global or national campaigns
methodOfCalculation: Sum of participants engaged across all campaigns (online and offline).
methods: Campaign reports, advocacy reports, participation records.
notes: Participants may include event attendees, online participants, petition signatories, or campaign volunteers.
